chunks: What Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, from al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAbd al-Salām, from Abū Ḥanīfah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about crying during salat (prayer): does it invalidate the salat (prayer)? He said: If he cries due to the remembrance of jannah (paradise) or nar (hellfire), then that is among the best of deeds in salat (prayer). But if it is because he remembered a deceased person of his, then his salat (prayer) is invalid.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ الْأَعْمَالِ: among the most virtuous acts performed in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) being discussed in terms of validity
key_terms.جَنَّةٍ: paradise, whose remembrance causes commendable weeping
key_terms.مَيِّتًا: a deceased person whose remembrance here leads to worldly grief
key_terms.نَارٍ: hellfire, whose remembrance causes commendable weeping

ai.seo_question: Does crying during salat (prayer) invalidate the prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about crying during salat (prayer). Crying out of remembrance of jannah (paradise) or nar (hellfire) is praised and counted among the best acts within salat (prayer), while crying due to personal worldly grief over a deceased person invalidates the salat (prayer).
